plan.title: feat(escalation): notify the operator when a worker stops on an operator-only step

narratives.Description: When a worker stops on a step only the operator can do, such as a mint or a hook deny that needs a human grant, nothing tells the operator, and stops sat 17 to 26 minutes before anyone noticed them on a consumer project. The escalation queue exists but nothing records these stops automatically and nothing delivers them. This story records each operator-only stop with the exact command and, when the operator turns it on, sends one desktop notification that lists every waiting step.
narratives.Overview:
1. Add one core helper that records an operator-only stop through `fileEscalation`, and only when `operatorNotify` is not `off` (with the notifier off it writes nothing): mints as `approval` with `dangerous: true`, other steps as `cmd_approval`, the exact command and worktree path in the body. It dedupes on (code, target, session) by exclusive-create of a key file, swallows its own errors, and never changes a verdict. relieves: P2
2. Call it from the PreToolUse deny for operator-remedy codes (the `authz-grant-*` codes, which also cover a push without a grant), beside `recordAuthzAudit`, and from `refuseNonInteractiveMint` on the agent-marker branch only, with its four callers passing argv and project root. `deft escalation:file` accepts a repeated `--command` for the code-less stops (fenced CHANGELOG line, `hotfix` label, operator disposition), and the preamble names that call as the residual path. relieves: P1
3. When `plan.policy.operatorNotify` is `os` (default `off`; USER.md Personal `operatorNotify` wins), a detached child with a timeout and no inherited stdin takes a notify lock under `.deft/escalations/` with the owner-token and liveness rules of `packages/core/src/plan-sequence/mutation-lock.ts` (no takeover while the owner is alive or unknown, release only by the holding token), collects every open, un-notified escalation for the project root, writes `.deft/escalations/.notified/<id>` for each, sends one OS notification listing them, rescans until none is left, and releases. A child that finds the lock held by a live owner waits on that acquisition loop until release, then takes the lock and sends whatever is still un-notified (nothing, if the holder already sent it). The payload is passed as data only (on Windows through a file or stdin, never a `-Command` string), every command is labelled agent-proposed, control characters are stripped, mint lines are shown one per line, and non-mint commands join into one script. relieves: P3
4. Fixtures: an agent-marker mint refusal records one `approval` escalation and fires the notifier once with the full command; two stops on disk produce one notification listing both, including when two notifier children start together; a stalled owner keeps the lock, a second reaper does not take it, an old owner cannot release a newer lock, and a stop filed after the holder's last rescan and before its release still appears in a notification; a repeated identical deny records once; notifier `off` writes no escalation, key or notify file and leaves output byte-identical; a URL-shaped value for the channel is refused; a human TTY mint typo records nothing.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator running agents, I want a desktop notification with the exact command when a worker stops on a step only I can do, so that stops do not sit unnoticed.

Spec-path: packages/core/src/escalation/ (fileEscalation + new notify) + packages/runtime/src/human-presence-mint.ts (refuseNonInteractiveMint)

## In plain English
When a worker stops on a step only a human can do, it should say so out loud. Prefer-A: the stop is written to the existing escalation queue with the exact command to run, and a small notifier, off by default, tells the operator as soon as it is written. Stops close together from one worker go out as one message with one script. The notifier only tells; it never runs the step, and no gate changes.

## Evidence (pin 1fa8ab9cc7b1aad651e6d65e4103f7820bde3d04)
- [types.ts L9-16, L75-92](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/1fa8ab9cc7b1aad651e6d65e4103f7820bde3d04/packages/core/src/escalation/types.ts#L9-L92): `cmd_approval` and `approval` exist; the event has `body` and `contextRefs` but no command field.
- [fileEscalation actions.ts L48](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/1fa8ab9cc7b1aad651e6d65e4103f7820bde3d04/packages/core/src/escalation/actions.ts#L48) is the one recorder; its only production caller is the `escalation:file` CLI (`packages/runtime/src/escalation-cli.ts:214`). Nothing records a stop automatically, and no notifier, webhook or OS-notification code exists in `packages/*/src`.
- [refuseNonInteractiveMint human-presence-mint.ts L207-267](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/1fa8ab9cc7b1aad651e6d65e4103f7820bde3d04/packages/runtime/src/human-presence-mint.ts#L207-L267) is the shared refusal for `authz:grant`, `scope:record-approved-scope`, `scope:record-intent-constraint` and `scope:record-observable-scope`; it knows the verb, so it can build the exact command.
- Precedence precedent: `resolveForgeOutageRetryMinutes` (`packages/core/src/policy/forge-outage-retry.ts:149`) reads USER.md Personal, then `plan.policy`, then a default.

## Draft remedy
1. Record: `refuseNonInteractiveMint` files one `cmd_approval` escalation whose body holds the exact command line to run. Workers stopping on other operator-only steps (fenced CHANGELOG line, `hotfix` label, default-branch push) file through the existing `deft escalation:file --type cmd_approval`, with the command or script in the body; the worker preamble names that call at every BLOCKED operator stop.
2. Notify: after `fileEscalation` saves, when `plan.policy.operatorNotify.enabled` is true, a notifier delivers title plus command. Channels: `os` (default: Windows toast, macOS `osascript`, Linux `notify-send`), `webhook` (URL read only from USER.md Personal or an environment variable, never from tracked `plan.policy`). USER.md Personal `operatorNotifyChannel` wins over `plan.policy`. Delivery failure is logged and never fails the caller.
3. Batch: escalations from the same agent id within a short quiet window (default 30 s) go out as one notification that lists every command as one script; each escalation records `notifiedAt` so nothing is sent twice.
4. Fixtures: mint refusal records one escalation and fires the notifier once with the command; two stops in one window send one notification listing both; notifier off leaves behaviour and output byte-identical; a webhook URL in `plan.policy` is refused at policy validation.

## Not proposed
No gate, hook or mint behaviour changes; the notifier never performs a step. No host-specific channel in this cut (a host notification surface can be a later channel). No new escalation type.

Round 1, inclusive ceiling 6856998346, pin `1fa8ab9cc7b1aad651e6d65e4103f7820bde3d04` (verified HEAD). I read the supplied thread snapshot, critique rules, escalation implementation and contract, mint refusal and callers, hook denial/audit paths, policy precedence implementation, and worker preamble. Verification was read-only source inspection; no network, builds, edits, or posts.

## Verdict

Prefer-A reuses the right queue, but cannot bind as written. Its automatic recording point misses earlier stops, its batching promise lacks a process owner, and its outbound handling leaves command data and delivery semantics underspecified. A smaller first cut—explicit per-step filing with bounded notification delivery—can address P1–P3 without changing authority.

## F1 - blocks-the-design: Mint refusal is not the common stop boundary

`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1852` records authorization audit and returns a denial before the requested tool executes; `deny` at line 1343 merely constructs a decision. Neither files an escalation. Moreover, `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md:30` tells unattended workers to park pending a human mint, and line 31 forbids pasting mint argv into the agent shell. A compliant worker need never reach `refuseNonInteractiveMint`. Even CLI callers can return earlier: `packages/runtime/src/authz.ts:394` and `scope-record-approved-scope.ts:268` check active UAT first.

Thus the mint fixture does not establish P1 coverage. Change the remedy to make explicit filing apply to **every** operator-only stop, including pre-execution denial and planned parking, with automatic mint recording only supplemental. Name the covered denial classes and verify the filing command remains reachable under those conditions. Preserve denial results when recording fails; do not turn every retryable denial into an operator notification.

## F2 - blocks-the-design: Knowing the verb cannot produce the exact command

`packages/runtime/src/human-presence-mint.ts:207` receives a verb, confirmation flag, and presence seams—not project root, scope arguments, target, or command payload. The richer context remains in callers, such as `scope-record-approved-scope.ts:264` and `scope-record-intent-constraint.ts:149`. The claimed inference “knows the verb, so it can build the exact command” is false; P2 would still require a round trip.

Pass a caller-prepared remediation description containing working directory, shell dialect, and safely quoted arguments, or file where that context exists. Do not reconstruct commands from refusal prose. Distinguish a runnable command from a human decision requiring missing information.

## F3 - blocks-the-design: Quiet-window batching has no owner or reliable identity

`packages/core/src/escalation/actions.ts:48` is synchronous save-and-return; `packages/runtime/src/escalation-cli.ts:348` assigns the synchronous main result to `process.exitCode`. No proposed component owns the thirty-second window after these short-lived invocations finish. Keeping each invocation alive instead delays sequential filing and permits competing senders. Both `actions.ts:58` and `escalation-cli.ts:49` default identity to `"agent"`, so unrelated workers can also be combined.

Replace time-window batching with one explicit per-step escalation containing the ordered commands, filed once after collecting known blockers. This directly addresses P3 without a daemon. Quiet-window aggregation better accommodates independently arriving stops, but would require an explicit durable scheduler, unique project/worktree/worker/step identity, and concurrency rules; that larger design would change this recommendation.

## F4 - blocks-the-design: Secret destination handling does not protect the payload

`packages/core/src/escalation/store.ts:119` accepts arbitrary body text; `actions.ts:61` preserves it. Sending title plus command therefore exports potentially secret arguments or untrusted instructions even when the webhook URL itself stays outside tracked policy. OS adapters implemented through shell or AppleScript interpolation could also execute payload fragments, violating the invariant.

Specify data-only adapters, no shell evaluation or executable notification actions, bounded delivery time, and sanitized diagnostics that never expose endpoint credentials. Keep secret-bearing commands local and send a safe summary plus escalation reference. Define USER.md-versus-environment endpoint precedence and prohibit silent fallback to another destination. The numeric fallback precedent at `packages/core/src/policy/forge-outage-retry.ts:149` does not establish safe routing semantics for outbound data.

## F5 - blocks-the-design: `notifiedAt` neither survives current parsing nor guarantees once

## Summary

When a worker reaches a step only a human can do (a mint, a CHANGELOG line the fence refuses, a `hotfix` label, a push to the default branch, a disposition in the operator's name), it stops and waits. Nothing tells the operator. The typed escalation queue (`packages/core/src/escalation/`, `.deft/escalations/`, #518) holds the event, but nothing delivers it.

## Consumer impact

On a consumer project, the operator was stopped six times in one change and waited on for about 85 minutes. Three stops sat 17-26 minutes each before anyone noticed them.

## Expected

- An operator-only stop records a typed escalation (existing schema; an `approval` or `cmd_approval` type), with the exact command or script the operator must run.
- A configurable notifier delivers it as soon as it is recorded: an OS notification by default, an optional webhook (for example Slack), and the host's own notification channel where the host provides one. Set in `plan.policy`, off by default, with USER.md Personal winning for the channel.
- Stops that happen together in one step go out as one notification with one script, not one by one.
- No gate changes: the notification carries the step; it never performs it.

## Acceptance

- Given a worker that reaches a mint step, when the escalation is recorded, then the configured notifier fires once with the command to run.
- Given two operator-only steps in the same step, then one notification lists both.
- With the notifier off, behaviour is unchanged.

Refs #518.
